title: Picture to Part
tagline: I hand it a picture. My printer gets a part that already fits.
what: Code I wrote that turns a flat picture, like a logo, a pattern or a label, into a solid 3D shape and carves it into a part for my 3D printer. I used it to dress up the small printed rack that holds my home server: lattice vents, clear side panels, nameplates.
built: Wrote the code that turns a two-color picture into a printable part, no CAD app open
Cut a 526-hole lattice into a flat panel and checked the solid had no gaps
Got clear plastic to print glass-clear, so the art sits inside a see-through panel
Set 8 checks every part passes before printing
credit: My code, dressing up other people's rack parts
starring: The rack that holds my home server
progress: Printed so far: clear side panels, fan caps, a power-supply plate, drive trays and a fan panel

making.problem: I wanted the little printed rack for my home server to look like mine. I don't do CAD, so I needed code that puts my art onto parts that already fit.
how: Start from a picture: a logo, a pattern or a label in two colors
Trace it into clean shapes and turn those into a solid with no gaps
Carve it into an existing part, matching its size to within 0.01 mm
Run 8 checks, render it, look at it, then send it to the printer
credits: The Lab Rax rack and other donor parts, shared on MakerWorld by their designers
The clear-print settings come from the How to Print Ice profile on MakerWorld
Built on manifold3d, Shapely, OpenCV and trimesh. Some source art began as AI-generated images

moment.what: The rack's vent pieces came with a honeycomb grid. I cut out just the grid, grew a Japanese asanoha lattice in its place, and left the original designer's logo alone, with the new struts fused 0.8 mm into it.

b: Black art on a red badge
